key_cases.case_name: Raboin v. North Dakota Department of Human Services
key_cases.holding: The court held that a Department determination of probable cause to believe child abuse is indicated affects legal rights and is an appealable final order, and that on this record the determination was not supported by a preponderance of the evidence, reversing and remanding with directions to vacate the probable-cause finding.
key_cases.relevance: The intake-to-investigation machinery described applies to hotline and anonymous reports.
key_cases.quote: We conclude there is a statutory right of appeal to the courts from the Department's finding of probable cause to believe child abuse or neglect is indicated.

key_cases.case_name: K.D. v. County of Crow Wing
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit
key_cases.holding: Affirming summary judgment for county and city defendants, the court held that removal of a child without a court order is constitutionally permitted only where continued parental custody poses an imminent threat, that officials acting on a reasonable suspicion of abuse have qualified immunity, and that after such a removal the state must promptly initiate judicial proceedings.
key_cases.relevance: Governs action taken on an unverified tip where no imminent threat can be articulated.
key_cases.quote: In cases in which continued parental custody poses an imminent threat to the child's health or welfare, emergency removal of children without a court order is constitutionally permitted.

mandatory_reporters: Listed professionals only — North Dakota is not a universal-reporting state (N.D. Cent. Code § 50-25.1-03(1))
Tier 1, 2, 3, and 4 mental health professionals (as defined in N.D. Cent. Code § 25-01-01) and any other medical or mental health professional
Religious practitioners of the healing arts
Schoolteachers, school administrators, and school counselors
Child care workers and child care licensors
Juvenile court personnel and probation officers
Licensed social workers and family service specialists
Members of the clergy, except when the knowledge is derived from information received as a spiritual adviser
Any person who discovers images of sexual conduct by a child on a workplace computer (N.D. Cent. Code § 50-25.1-03(3))
reporting_details: North Dakota is not a universal-reporting state: the professionals listed in N.D. Cent. Code § 50-25.1-03(1) must immediately report orally or in writing to the Department of Health and Human Services or its authorized agent, while any other person may report (N.D. Cent. Code §§ 50-25.1-03(2), 50-25.1-04(1)).

other: A child placed for care or adoption in violation of law

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediately if there is a serious threat to the child's life or health; otherwise within department-set time frames

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: An extension of time must be requested of and granted by the department (N.D. Admin. Code § 75-03-19-04).
